intro.title: Reusable Button
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Button component in React. You'll learn how to create a component that accepts props to customize its text and appearance, making it flexible for use across different parts of an application. The core concept is component reusability, which allows you to write efficient, maintainable code by avoiding duplication. You'll use JSX for structure, JavaScript functions to define the component, and props to pass data into it. By the end, you'll have a button that can be easily adapted with different labels and styles.
intro.usecase: Reusable buttons are foundational UI components found in nearly every web application. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon, consistent buttons handle 'Add to Cart', 'Buy Now', and 'Save for Later' actions across product pages. Dashboard applications like Salesforce use reusable buttons for 'Save', 'Submit', and 'Export' operations to maintain visual consistency. Form-heavy applications such as banking portals rely on reusable buttons for 'Transfer', 'Pay', and 'Cancel' actions to ensure predictable user interactions. This pattern allows developers to maintain consistent styling and behavior while reducing code duplication across complex interfaces.
